correction_2026_10_10: R7's SUPPRESSION IS SUPERSEDED FOR THIS SHAPE, and the reason it existed is why the replacement is honest. R7 dropped the row rather than rewriting the target, because every alternative claims something false — `map calls ApiError` says a call is a call OF the type, and promoting to `instantiates` would extend DT-A's in-file named-constructor evidence to a cross-file guess. What the receiver-type spelling publishes instead is neither of those: `load calls RemoteFailure.unknown` names the named constructor's OWNER and its segment, which is what the source writes and what the analyzer can point at, and it carries `baseBeyondRunScope: RemoteFailure` — the declared cause saying the run could not look the owner up, which the gate reads only where the target names nothing. So the row is no longer an unpublishable placeholder (`unknown` alone names nothing anywhere) nor a false claim about the type. THE TWO REJECTED ALTERNATIVES STAY REJECTED and are still forbidden below, which is the whole difference between this change and reopening R7: `load calls RemoteFailure` and `instantiates load -> RemoteFailure` remain false statements about a call, and the bare leaf `unknown` remains a placeholder that no declaration answers.
rationale: PINS M60 rule R7 for this lane: no relationship of any label may carry the placeholder literal `unknown` as an endpoint. Measured before the fix over 1,000 corpus files in 5 repositories: 19 such rows, all of the shape `ApiError.unknown('...')` — a selector chain reduced to its leaf, where the leaf of a constructor call on a capitalized type is the named constructor's segment and the segment is the word `unknown`. The published edge read `map calls unknown`, an endpoint no file in the sample declares (0 symbols named `unknown` in the same 1,000 files). The fix drops the row rather than rewriting the target, because every alternative claims something false: `map calls ApiError` says a call is a call OF the type, and promoting to `instantiates` would extend DT-A's in-file named-constructor evidence to a cross-file guess. The last expectation row pins the ADJACENT convention that is deliberately left alone (a cross-file named constructor with any other segment still publishes a leaf call), because the fix must be read as suppressing an unpublishable claim rather than as a blanket refusal — and because that surviving row is a declared limitation, recorded here so a later change to it is deliberate. That later change happened on 2026-10-10 and is recorded above (correction_2026_10_10): the adjacent convention's row is now SPELLED, and the suppressed row returns with its owner named.

expectRelationships.note: THE CONTROL, and it is in the same method as the suppressed rows: an ordinary cross-method call still publishes, so this fixture cannot pass by the method having published nothing.

THE IN-FILE HALF, and the row that separates the fix from muting. `ApiError.unknown(raw)` is the SAME source shape as the suppressed `RemoteFailure.unknown(...)`; because `ApiError` is declared here, DT-A's named-constructor rule applies and the construction publishes as `instantiates` to the RECEIVER — not to the segment. A fix that dropped every named-constructor edge would fail this row.

A control outside `load`, so the run cannot satisfy the control pair with one lucky method. SPELLED 2026-10-10: `raw.trim()` where `raw` is a String names the SDK type the run cannot see, so the target carries it and the claim says why nothing in this run could confirm it.

THE ADJACENT CONVENTION, NOW SPELLED (was `target: parsing`, pinned as a declared limitation since R7 and explicitly NOT endorsed there). `RemoteFailure.parsing(...)` is a cross-file named constructor, and the leaf-call convention published `parsing`, which resolves to nothing because constructors publish under the family name `constructor`. Naming the owner is strictly more informative and the claim keeps it honest.

THE ROW R7 SUPPRESSED, back as a published edge with its owner named. It is here so the change to R7's behaviour is a POSITIVE pin rather than an absence nobody looks for: the placeholder `unknown` is still forbidden (below), `RemoteFailure` alone is still forbidden, and the `instantiates` promotion is still forbidden — what changed is only that the edge can now name the owner and the segment the source wrote.

forbidRelationships.note: THE R7 PIN, UNCHANGED. `type` is deliberately absent, so this row matches an endpoint pair under ANY label: the corpus defect appeared as `calls`, and a pass that emitted it as `references` or `uses` would satisfy every other row in this file. The spelling does not weaken it — `RemoteFailure.unknown` is a different endpoint from `unknown`.
The corpus row verbatim, pinned again with its label so the regression is recognisable as the shape it was rather than as an endpoint pair.

THE ALTERNATIVE THAT WAS REJECTED. Publishing `load calls RemoteFailure` would give the edge a resolvable-looking target, and it is a false claim: a call is not a call OF the type. An edge that resolves is not thereby true, and this row is what says so — it is ALSO what keeps the 2026-10-10 change from being a reopening of R7: the change names the CONSTRUCTOR (`RemoteFailure.unknown`), never the type alone.

AND THE OTHER REJECTED ALTERNATIVE. `RemoteFailure` is declared in another file, so nothing here is evidence that `.unknown` is a constructor; promoting the row to `instantiates` on a guess would add an edge no oracle derives and that `bb_impact` would then report as a construction site.
2026-10-10 — the superseded leaf shape for the adjacent-convention row, forbidden so the spelling and the leaf convention cannot both be live.
